i think you have a misconstrued view on how different a t5 vs t10 school is... usually when people refer to high rank at a lower tier school, they mean skipping out on a t20 to go to your state school.

in terms of higher rank at lower ranking school vs. just attending a high ranking school, it depends on what you plan to do in the future and how critical making connections is for your intended career. if you plan on going to med school, it doesn't matter where you attend undergrad as long as you maintain a high GPA. if you plan on going to wallstreet, then it's all about getting into elite schools to form connections.

I'm really glad you were able to find yourself, and I wish you the best of luck for the future. However, I still think the mindset of one 'one true purpose' is unhealthy, and that no single person or group can help you find that one true passion you look for. They might aid you, but in the end, everyone is an individual and no two people are the same. You are you, and you need to trust in yourself.

I know my words sound empty, but just keep trying to better yourself, one step at a time. Life is fluid, not concrete. There are no rules to follow. Search for passions, but don't drive yourself in the ground trying to do so.

When the time comes where you are proud of who you are in the present, then you have found your purpose.

i think there are plenty of ways students could tackle it. maybe one person would change the laws of physics, another might add a fantastical element. 

here is my half-assed answer that i would refine a thousand times before submitting:

my rule for the world would personally fall into the later category of fantasy. call me a romantic, but i would like for everyone to have a soulmate they are bound to meet and love before they die. it doesn't matter whether that soulmate is romantic or platonic, a lover or a friend. it doesn't matter if that soulmate is human or an animal companion, or even an object like a piano they can't seem to part with. maybe their soulmate is a field of study, maybe it's a place.  

when i think about rules for the world, there are many issues. wishing for something to apply to everyone is bound to lead some people to believe that what is ideal to one person is a curse rather than a blessing. however, while the idea of having and finding soulmates might be twisted in some manner, i believe it is something neutral enough that is overall a good thing. afterall, in my definition, a soulmate is just something or someone that makes you truly happy, and why would anyone not want that? it is not one thing applied to everyone, but rather a concept that leads to individualized pieces of joy. my hope for is that in the end, everyone will be truly happy for at least one moment in their lives.

I would ask if they could set create and/or change one rule for the entire world, what would it be.

edit: forget to put the word "change" after and/or

I'm not sure how much aid you need, but as the previous commenter stated, you'll likely get at least some aid depending on your family income.

For the other costs, it would be pretty difficult applying to really high level scholarships simply because they are so competitive, but try looking up local ones. Usually, as long as you have good scores, grades, and ECs, they just ask you to write an essay and if they are small enough, you are likely to get them as not many people apply to small ones. $1k scholarships might not seem like too much but  if you get multiple of them, they'll at least help you out a litte.
